I always found the argument that someone not eating or throwing away part of a meal that they had not finished as helping support starving people on the other side of the planet laughable. The issue isn't the amount of food that we waste, but rather the access or lack of access to food that people in starving areas receive. Us having an abundance of food and no longer wasting any food isn't going to make other people on a separate continent starve any less. You'd need to have a coordinated effort to assist said people.

Besides that, I understand where many people are getting at when they talk about fixing hams by increasing taxes, a common argument made by hams is that what they do to themselves do not affect others. On a grand scale of things we can see that the obesity epidemic for example significantly impacts the healthcare industry. It's very clear that what they're doing to themselves is indeed affecting others even if it's indirect, we can also see in some nations that people who are merely obese can be classified as disabled and thus receive benefits that could be going to actual disabled individuals. Or the famous Food Stamp Fatties.

However, I do disagree with many people in some cases, for example an individual ham that goes to the store to buy a massive amount of food with their own earned money is hardly 'stealing' - it is disgusting but I don't see it as stealing. I mean we can get into an argument that says by them buying all that excess food for themselves they help cut out a significant portion of the food supply and blah blah, but the amount of hoops we have jump through to say that said person buying extra food with their own money caused the death of a starving person on the other side of the planet is ridiculous.

If someone buys something with their own earned money, they're not stealing anything.

If a ham goes around getting tons of food stamps and gorges itself when those food stamps could be going to other people is a different story in my opinion.
